notes: ETF holdings persistence, schemas, services, API routes, migration, scheduled refresh hook, and Chart holdings panel are implemented.

Manual row ingestion, CSV ingestion, configured public CSV URL refresh, coverage summary, point-in-time nearest lookup, unresolved holdings, and constituent timeline APIs with per-point weight deltas are covered by focused backend tests.

Strategy Lab can use ETF holdings snapshots as static universes for coverage preview and backtest execution; the visual builder can also opt rules backtests into dynamic point-in-time ETF holdings membership with universe_config.etf_holdings.snapshot_mode = dynamic, choose whether constituent removals leave positions open or realize constituent_removed exits, and inspect baseline snapshot attribution in dynamic run summaries/execution logs and the Strategy Lab execution-log UI.
ETF holdings snapshots can materialize read-only system-managed baskets through the basket backend model and APIs.

Manual basket CRUD now exists on the backend with existing-instrument validation, duplicate rejection, custom-weight sum validation, read-only system-basket protection, and auto sector/industry classification.

Strategy Lab can use manual or ETF-derived baskets as static universes through universe_config.basket_id; ETF-derived system baskets can opt into dynamic source ETF holdings history and manual baskets can opt into persisted basket composition-history replay with universe_config.basket_snapshot_mode = dynamic; these paths have visual-builder save/load and focused integration coverage.
The Chart holdings panel and Strategy Lab ETF universe builder path are covered by frontend unit tests, and the frontend type-check passes.

The Chart ETF holdings panel now supports selected-holding mini-stats, previous/next navigation through filtered holdings, source/resolution metadata inspection, and explicit constituent open actions.
A dedicated /etf-holdings workspace now lists ETFs with stored holdings and loads holdings rows through a server-side paginated/searchable/sortable API for large-list browsing.
The /etf-holdings workspace now includes a first cross-snapshot diff view so users can compare two stored snapshots for additions, removals, and weight changes.

The ETF holdings diff workspace now also surfaces first-pass churn/reweight research summaries, including gross churn, added/removed weight, upweights/downweights, and largest additions/removals/reweights.
The /etf-holdings workspace now includes a first top-mover weight-evolution view across stored snapshots.

The /etf-holdings workspace now includes a turnover timeline that batch-navigates adjacent historical snapshots and summarizes churn, additions, removals, reweights, and top movers for each transition.

ETF holdings overlap summaries now compare selected ETF snapshots for shared/unique constituents, Jaccard overlap, shared weights, minimum-overlap weight, and top shared holdings, with a compact ETF holdings workspace panel for selecting peer ETFs from the loaded profile list.

Many-ETF overlap matrix analytics now exist through POST /api/v1/etf-holdings/overlap-matrix, including row/column ETF symbols, matrix cells, closest/most-distinct peers, and highest/lowest overlap pair callouts.
Overlap matrix requests can now expand ETF participants from profile metadata such as issuer, fund family, and search query, instead of requiring every ETF symbol to be listed manually.
The ETF holdings workspace now surfaces a compact heatmap-style overlap matrix alongside pairwise overlap cards, plus first issuer/family/search controls for server-side matrix expansion.
ETF constituent timeline API points now expose weight_delta_from_previous so individual constituent reweighting paths can be inspected without client-side recomputation.
Strategy Lab basket universe selection is covered by frontend unit tests, and focused basket backend integration tests pass.
The current usable free-source path is configured public holdings CSV/XLSX/ZIP URLs stored in ETF profile provider_aliases.
Basket builder/editor UI now exists at /baskets, reachable from the sidebar, with equal/custom weighting and read-only ETF-derived basket display.
Backend basket synthetic OHLCV now exists as a rebased-to-100 weighted return series endpoint.
Chart can open BASKET:{id} synthetic basket tokens from the basket builder and loads them through the basket OHLCV endpoint without treating them as normal watchlist/recent instruments.
ETF holdings refresh now uses an adapter registry seam; configured public CSV URLs are fetched through the registered adapter interface.
SEC N-PORT/N-PORT-P-style XML parsing/admin ingestion now exists as a filing-reconstructed holdings primitive.
SEC EDGAR recent and archived-submissions N-PORT backfill now exists as an admin API primitive for ETF profiles with sec_cik.
SEC backfill jobs and accession-level filing state are persisted; duplicate accessions are skipped on rerun and job/filing state can be inspected through admin APIs.
Bulk and scheduled SEC N-PORT backfill orchestration exists behind bounded admin endpoint/task configuration.
Screener and Radar can consume manual or ETF-derived baskets as backend universe inputs.
Screener and Radar now expose frontend controls for selected manual or ETF-derived basket universes.

Issuer-aware CSV adapter routes now resolve from ETF profile URLs, URL templates, issuer product ids, file-name hints, and inferred product-page templates; concrete issuer-specific route constructors now exist for ARK file-name CSV files, iShares/BlackRock product-id CSV files, and State Street/SPDR symbol-based daily holdings XLSX files.

Inferred issuer product-page templates now cover common symbol-addressable Vanguard, Invesco, Schwab, Global X, and VanEck pages; other issuers can still use explicit product URLs, issuer discovery feeds, or profile-level URL templates without new code.

Issuer-aware ETF holdings adapters can now discover linked CSV/XLSX/ZIP holdings files from configured issuer product/fund page URLs and still identity-validate the downloaded artifact before ingestion.
Issuer product-page discovery now scans anchor hrefs, conservative URL-bearing data attributes, and quoted page configuration strings while still requiring supported holdings-like file URLs.
ETF holdings adapter route readiness can be inspected through admin POST /api/v1/etf-holdings/{symbol}/probe-adapter and persisted in adapter-state health.

ETF holdings adapter health can be inspected through admin GET /api/v1/etf-holdings/{symbol}/adapter-state, including source/count/completeness metadata and HTTP rate-limit/blocking classification for failed refreshes; stale rate-limit state is cleared on successful retry.
ETF holdings adapter inference now uses configured ETF profile/product/holdings URL domains as confidence-scored issuer signals while preserving the no ticker-only guessing rule.

Issuer ETF holdings adapters now support explicit dated URL templates and admin POST /api/v1/etf-holdings/{symbol}/refresh-date for one-date historical fetch/ingest when an issuer archive URL pattern is known.

ETF holdings adapter capabilities can be inspected through admin GET /api/v1/etf-holdings/adapters, including route identifiers, required identifiers, supported formats, parser confidence, dated-fetch support, and explicit configured discovery-feed support.

Issuer ETF holdings adapters now support explicit configured fund-list discovery feeds through admin POST /api/v1/etf-holdings/discover; CSV/XLSX/ZIP discovery feeds can materialize lightweight ETF instruments and upsert profiles with issuer product ids, holdings URLs/templates, dated URL templates, CUSIP/ISIN identifiers, SEC CIK/series/class ids, FIGI/composite/share-class FIGI aliases, discovery source metadata, and raw discovery-row audit data.

Fetched issuer artifacts can be identity-validated against explicit expected ETF/fund symbol, name, CUSIP, or ISIN before ingestion; mismatches fail refresh and matched/unverified status is stored in legal metadata.

Fetched issuer CSV/XLSX table artifacts can also infer ETF identity from conservative metadata such as two-column preambles and explicit fund/ETF identity columns; generic constituent ticker columns are ignored.

Simple XLSX/OpenXML issuer holdings workbooks and ZIP archives containing CSV/XLSX holdings files now ingest through the same adapter path as CSV files, preserving source-format metadata and raw table payloads.

ETF holdings source-hardening baseline now exists: malformed/empty issuer files fail refresh and persist adapter failure state; common issuer schema aliases, CUSIP-like security identifiers, cash rows, accounting negatives, and non-holding disclaimer rows are handled; and SEC legacy parsing covers XML/table filings, simple HTML tables, split identity/value rows, month-name dates, and value-in-thousands schedules.

Opt-in live ETF holdings provider tests now pass against current backend-reachable public issuer routes for SPDR, iShares, Global X, and VanEck; ARK, Vanguard, and Schwab remain explicit provider-support gaps until current backend-reachable routes/APIs are implemented.
ETF holdings row API outputs now expose the persisted per-snapshot source_row_hash for audit/replay tooling.
Baseline manual/admin legacy SEC N-Q/N-CSR-style XML/table and simple EDGAR HTML schedule-table reconstruction now exists as sec_legacy_reconstructed_holdings provenance.
Legacy SEC HTML parsing now supports split-row schedule tables where the security identity/CUSIP row is followed by a separate numeric shares/value/percent row.
Automated SEC legacy N-Q/N-CSR-style EDGAR discovery/download/backfill now exists with duplicate-safe accession state, single-ETF endpoint, bulk endpoint, and focused integration coverage.

SEC company_tickers_mf-style fund ticker discovery now exists through admin POST /api/v1/etf-holdings/discover-sec-funds; it materializes lightweight ETF instruments and upserts SEC CIK/series/class ids for EDGAR backfill routing, with optional source_url override and keyed-object/fields-data payload support.

Remaining ETF holdings work is now downstream consumption and long-tail maintenance rather than a core source-hardening gap: unusual issuer-specific schemas, non-tabular/PDF-like disclosures, automatic/broad issuer ETF discovery beyond explicit configured fund-list feeds, deeper dynamic point-in-time ETF attribution drilldowns, richer basket-history editing/import/rebalance policy UX, deeply nested/footnoted SEC HTML or PDF-like filings, saved ETF comparison sets/clustering UX on top of the overlap matrix API, and richer basket chart semantics remain explicit follow-up work.
